buttons.name: MakeMasksUploadDataButton

Btn contribute

Send the image on screen with its mask, every image you have curated here, or an images folder with a masks folder holding masks of the same names. Say what they show (organism, object type, stain) and they go to their own community dataset on Hugging Face as a pull request, which the maintainer reviews before any model is trained on it. They are shared under CC BY 4.0, so send only images you have the right to share. A careful mask makes a good model: every object, hugging its edge.

buttons.name: MakeMasksBoxTool
buttons.tooltip:
Mode buttons box
Draw YOLO bounding boxes (X). Drag inside to move, drag a corner to resize, or right-click to delete. Ctrl-drag draws an overlapping box.
Open spaCR API documentation

Mode buttons recrop
Drag a box round one object and that region of the image and the mask becomes a field of its own, queued straight after this one. Objects the box cuts through are dropped. The field you cut them from is moved into recropped_originals/ when you move on, not deleted.
Open spaCR API documentation

Mode buttons ruler
Drag a line to measure its length in image pixels. Right-click with Ruler selected to clear it. Zoom and pan preserve the measurement.
Open spaCR API documentation

Btn cellpose
Segment the open field with the Object detection model and fold the result in as the replace/merge setting says. Fills the Cell probability and Flows tabs with what the run was thinking.
Open spaCR API documentation

Btn settings
Show or hide the settings — brush, wand, display, auto-filter, object operations, Otsu, object detection and the live magnifier, as one group. The canvas takes the width they give up.
Open spaCR API documentation

Btn magnifier
Show a box under the mouse with the region around it magnified and the objects a model finds in it outlined. A click adds them to the mask as new objects — under Whole image, only the object clicked — one undo step per click. While it is on, the mouse wheel changes the box's zoom rather than the view's.
Open spaCR API documentation

buttons.name: ConsoleCopyGlyph
buttons.tooltip: Copy this section, header and all

Wand relative
On: the tolerance below is a percentage of THIS image's own intensity range, so one setting behaves the same on 8-bit and 16-bit data. Off: a fixed grey-level distance, which selects nothing on a 16-bit image at a value tuned for 8-bit and floods the whole frame the other way round.
Open spaCR API documentation

buttons.text: Keep the nearest pixels at the cap
buttons.tooltip:
Wand salvage
On: a flood over the budget is trimmed back to the pixels reachable nearest the click, which leaves a bounded object you can edit. Off: an over-budget flood is refused outright and the mask is untouched, so a tolerance that is far too high says so instead of handing back a piece of the field.
Open spaCR API documentation

Wand intensity border
When a leak is found, search for the highest tolerance whose flood stays put and take that instead of the straight cut. The boundary is then drawn by the image's own intensities. Only helps when the seam is dimmer than the object; when it is exactly as bright, no tolerance separates them and the cut stands.
Open spaCR API documentation

Wand gradient taper
Let the provisional edge move onto the nearest real intensity change, inside the band below. This is what removes the last straight lines and circular arcs left by a cut or a budget.
Open spaCR API documentation

Btn levels
Set black and white cutoffs by dragging on the image histogram.
Open spaCR API documentation

Detect normalized
Off: Otsu, Cellpose and the magnifier read the image as it was loaded (inverted if Invert is on), and Lower % / Upper % only change how it is drawn. On: they read it stretched between Lower % and Upper %, exactly as drawn, and the intensity in the top-left corner shows that stretched value. What is saved is never changed.
Open spaCR API documentation

Invert display
Invert the picture and the pixels used for detection, so dark objects become bright. The field is normalized to 0..1, then each pixel becomes 1 minus itself. Hover pixel intensity follows the inversion; object mean intensity and Filter thresholds use the original loaded values. The loaded image data and existing mask are unchanged. To swap foreground and background in a finished mask, use 'Swap object and background' in Object operations.
Open spaCR API documentation

Filter add
Add a row for the property on the left, with a minimum and a maximum. A blank bound is off; an object outside a bound is hidden, and removing the row brings it back.
Open spaCR API documentation

Btn filter
Apply the filter list to the mask on screen again. Every object it hides is listed below it, with the value that hid it. One undo step.
Open spaCR API documentation

Control 46
Close every enclosed hole inside an object, so a nucleus outlined as a ring becomes a filled disc.
Open spaCR API documentation

Control 47
Renumber the objects 1, 2, 3… with no gaps. The picture does not change; the ids underneath it do.
Open spaCR API documentation

Control 48
Turn every labelled pixel into background and every background pixel into an object. On an ordinary field that gives ONE object covering the whole frame with holes where your objects were — useful only when you have outlined the space between the cells and wanted the cells. This is not the picture invert: that is 'Invert image', in the Display category, and it leaves the mask alone.
Open spaCR API documentation

buttons.name: ConsoleCopyGlyph
buttons.tooltip: Copy this section, header and all

Wand relative

buttons.text: Keep the nearest pixels at the cap
buttons.tooltip:
Wand salvage
On: a flood over the budget is trimmed back to the pixels reachable nearest the click, which leaves a bounded object you can edit. Off: an over-budget flood is refused outright and the mask is untouched, so a tolerance that is far too high says so instead of handing back a piece of the field.
Open spaCR API documentation

Wand intensity border
When a leak is found, search for the highest tolerance whose flood stays put and take that instead of the straight cut. The boundary is then drawn by the image's own intensities. Only helps when the seam is dimmer than the object; when it is exactly as bright, no tolerance separates them and the cut stands.
Open spaCR API documentation

Wand gradient taper
Let the provisional edge move onto the nearest real intensity change, inside the band below. This is what removes the last straight lines and circular arcs left by a cut or a budget.
Open spaCR API documentation

Btn levels
Set black and white cutoffs by dragging on the image histogram.
Open spaCR API documentation

Detect normalized
Off: Otsu, Cellpose and the magnifier read the image as it was loaded (inverted if Invert is on), and Lower % / Upper % only change how it is drawn. On: they read it stretched between Lower % and Upper %, exactly as drawn, and the intensity in the top-left corner shows that stretched value. What is saved is never changed.
Open spaCR API documentation

Invert display
Invert the picture and the pixels used for detection, so dark objects become bright. The field is normalized to 0..1, then each pixel becomes 1 minus itself. Hover pixel intensity follows the inversion; object mean intensity and Filter thresholds use the original loaded values. The loaded image data and existing mask are unchanged. To swap foreground and background in a finished mask, use 'Swap object and background' in Object operations.
Open spaCR API documentation

Filter add
Add a row for the property on the left, with a minimum and a maximum. A blank bound is off; an object outside a bound is hidden, and removing the row brings it back.
Open spaCR API documentation

Btn filter
Apply the filter list to the mask on screen again. Every object it hides is listed below it, with the value that hid it. One undo step.
Open spaCR API documentation

Control 46
Close every enclosed hole inside an object, so a nucleus outlined as a ring becomes a filled disc.
Open spaCR API documentation

Control 47
Renumber the objects 1, 2, 3… with no gaps. The picture does not change; the ids underneath it do.
Open spaCR API documentation

Control 48
Turn every labelled pixel into background and every background pixel into an object. On an ordinary field that gives ONE object covering the whole frame with holes where your objects were — useful only when you have outlined the space between the cells and wanted the cells. This is not the picture invert: that is 'Invert image', in the Display category, and it leaves the mask alone.

Mode buttons ruler

Btn settings
Show or hide the settings — brush, wand, display, auto-filter, object operations, Otsu, object detection and the live magnifier, as one group. The canvas takes the width they give up.
Open spaCR API documentation

Btn magnifier
Show a box under the mouse with the region around it magnified and the objects a model finds in it outlined. A click adds them to the mask as new objects — under Whole image, only the object clicked — one undo step per click. While it is on, the mouse wheel changes the box's zoom rather than the view's.
Open spaCR API documentation

buttons.name: ConsoleCopyGlyph
buttons.tooltip: Copy this section, header and all

Wand relative
On: the tolerance below is a percentage of THIS image's own intensity range, so one setting behaves the same on 8-bit and 16-bit data. Off: a fixed grey-level distance, which selects nothing on a 16-bit image at a value tuned for 8-bit and floods the whole frame the other way round.
Open spaCR API documentation

buttons.text: Keep the nearest pixels at the cap
buttons.tooltip:
Wand salvage
On: a flood over the budget is trimmed back to the pixels reachable nearest the click, which leaves a bounded object you can edit. Off: an over-budget flood is refused outright and the mask is untouched, so a tolerance that is far too high says so instead of handing back a piece of the field.
Open spaCR API documentation

Wand intensity border
When a leak is found, search for the highest tolerance whose flood stays put and take that instead of the straight cut. The boundary is then drawn by the image's own intensities. Only helps when the seam is dimmer than the object; when it is exactly as bright, no tolerance separates them and the cut stands.
Open spaCR API documentation

Wand gradient taper
Let the provisional edge move onto the nearest real intensity change, inside the band below. This is what removes the last straight lines and circular arcs left by a cut or a budget.
Open spaCR API documentation

Btn levels
Set black and white cutoffs by dragging on the image histogram.
Open spaCR API documentation

Detect normalized
Off: Otsu, Cellpose and the magnifier read the image as it was loaded (inverted if Invert is on), and Lower % / Upper % only change how it is drawn. On: they read it stretched between Lower % and Upper %, exactly as drawn, and the intensity in the top-left corner shows that stretched value. What is saved is never changed.
Open spaCR API documentation

Invert display
Invert the picture and the pixels used for detection, so dark objects become bright. The field is normalized to 0..1, then each pixel becomes 1 minus itself. Hover pixel intensity follows the inversion; object mean intensity and Filter thresholds use the original loaded values. The loaded image data and existing mask are unchanged. To swap foreground and background in a finished mask, use 'Swap object and background' in Object operations.
Open spaCR API documentation

Filter add
Add a row for the property on the left, with a minimum and a maximum. A blank bound is off; an object outside a bound is hidden, and removing the row brings it back.
Open spaCR API documentation

Btn filter
Apply the filter list to the mask on screen again. Every object it hides is listed below it, with the value that hid it. One undo step.
Open spaCR API documentation

Control 46
Close every enclosed hole inside an object, so a nucleus outlined as a ring becomes a filled disc.
Open spaCR API documentation

Control 47
Renumber the objects 1, 2, 3… with no gaps. The picture does not change; the ids underneath it do.
Open spaCR API documentation

Control 48
Turn every labelled pixel into background and every background pixel into an object. On an ordinary field that gives ONE object covering the whole frame with holes where your objects were — useful only when you have outlined the space between the cells and wanted the cells. This is not the picture invert: that is 'Invert image', in the Display category, and it leaves the mask alone.
Open spaCR API documentation
